headline: Revenue and profit keep climbing despite quieter markets
summary_short: Tradeweb's Q2 2026 revenue rose 9.0% y/y to $558.9M (down 9.5% q/q from an outsized Q1), with net income attributable to Tradeweb up 17.9% y/y to $181.3M ($0.85 diluted EPS), as broad-based gains in rates derivatives, credit, equities and market data offset a more normalized trading-volatility backdrop.
summary_long: Revenue growth was broad-based: rates (+10.2% y/y) led on higher derivatives and mortgage volumes, credit (+3.3%) on corporate-bond and derivatives volume partly offset by weaker municipals, equities (+13.5%) on derivatives and ETF activity, and market data (+22.6%) on an amended LSEG license agreement. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $304.1M (margin +24bps y/y to 54.4%) while Adjusted EBIT margin compressed 20bps to 50.6% on higher technology and data-infrastructure spend. Tradeweb's 10-Q states FY2026 capex/software-development guidance of $107-117M, up ~9% at the midpoint versus $103.1M spent in FY2025. The board declared a $0.14/share Q3 dividend and the company repurchased $188.9M of stock in the quarter; cash rose to $2,057.9M.

drivers.explanation: Broad-based revenue growth across rates, credit, equities, money markets and market data, plus a swing to net FX gains within G&A, drove profit higher despite a step-up in technology/data-infrastructure spend and a more normalized volatility backdrop.

The $46.0M increase was primarily driven by a $35.6M rise in transaction fees and commissions on higher volumes in rates derivatives, mortgages, corporate bonds, equity derivatives and ETFs, plus higher money-market commissions.
Tracks the 17.9% rise in net income attributable to Tradeweb, modestly amplified by a 1.0% reduction in diluted share count from ongoing buybacks.

Operating income grew as total expenses were roughly flat (+0.2% y/y): a 38.9% rise in technology/communications spend on data-infrastructure investment was offset by a 44.6% drop in G&A from a swing to net FX gains.

Beyond the operating-income gain, other income reflected unrealized gains on minority equity investments partly offset by unrealized Canton Coin losses, alongside a higher effective tax rate (23.5% vs 22.7%).

The 24bps y/y gain, per the company's own reconciliation, reflects Adjusted EBITDA growth (+9.4%) modestly outpacing revenue growth despite the technology-spend step-up; not separately narrated by the company.
Compression of 20bps is not separately narrated by the company beyond the reconciliation table; the same technology-spend increase affecting Adjusted EBITDA margin applies here.

Reflects $497.9M of six-month operating cash flow against $411.3M of financing outflows (buybacks, dividends, Tax Receivable Agreement payments) and $111.2M of investing outflows; not separately narrated by the company.

Growth is retained-earnings accretion from $386.6M of H1 net income attributable to Tradeweb, partly offset by $240.5M of H1 share repurchases and $59.5M of dividends paid; not separately narrated by the company.
Reflects $188.9M of Q2 share repurchases under the 2022 and 2026 Share Repurchase Programs, which the company states are conducted in part to offset annual dilution from stock-based compensation.
